selectionMethod: Provider recordings compared through decoded waveform/energy metrics and CLAP zero-shot relative-label screening; no human listening claimed. Browser output recorded after shared compressor.

sources: Exact provider responses and SHA256 metadata remain in provider-takes. Rejected takes are excluded from kitchen-bank and runtime.

scenarios.preserves: firm or berry pot contact; sustained stirring while held in pan and moving/physical decay; scoop on loading spoon; jam-flow during visible ribbon and jam-end on final thread; finish after accepted commit
scenarios.fruitAndBerryTarts: firm or berry contact selected from actual ingredient; sustained fine/coarse granular sugar during real swept sprinkle; stop on release; accepted finish
scenarios.honeyPear: actual pear cut contact; syrup stream while contacting pear; final drop on physical settling; accepted finish
scenarios.honeyBiscuits: knead contact and release; oven insertion on actual start, retrieval after bake; honey brush contact over actual dough surface; accepted finish
scenarios.honeyCake: continuous circular batter contact; oven start/end transitions; honey brush during glaze; accepted finish
scenarios.windParfait: custard scoop from bowl; cream-flow tracks actual transferred amount incl release drain; fruit glass contact; syrup stream; final drop; accepted finish
scenarios.grilledFish: salt continuous during actual grain placement; pan contact attack and continuous sizzle only at physics contact; actual turn; plated fish; separate solid carrot garnish; accepted finish
scenarios.workshopAndBread: continuous batter stir on real mixing; knead attack/release; rolling contact only while rolling owner touches and moves; successful geometric dough cut; accepted oven insertion/retrieval
scenarios.arrangement: physics impact material selected from cup/food/egg and table/basket; sounds gated until loaded; accepted completion

limits: CLAP scores depend on candidate labels and are a screening signal rather than a listener verdict.
Current jam animation emits a fixed approximately half-second ribbon for each successful scoop, so source is sustained for that exact visible interval; no artificial long pour is added.
